author: Eucherius of Lyon

passages.original: ita in sententiam nostram propositumque migravit, ut eliam cunctas admodum mundi partes eloquio operibusque resperserit.Jlilarius nuper, et in ltalia nunc antistes Petronius, ambo ex illa plenissima, ut aiunt, mundana; potestatis sede, unus in religionis, alius in sacerdotii nomen ascendit. Et quando clarissimos farundia, Firmianum, Minutium, Cyprianum, Ililarium [Pro Hilario reponendum Eram. censet Evagrium] Joannem [Sane Chrysostomum], Ambrosium, ex illo volumine numerositatis evolvam? Dixerant, credo, et hi sibi, quod quidam nostrum ait, cum se a saeculo in hanc beatiorem vitam, hoc velut stimulo concitaret: dixerant, credo, Quid hoc est?
passages.english: so passed over into our way of thinking and our purpose that he has even sprinkled all the parts of the world with his eloquence and his works. Hilary lately, and now in Italy the bishop Petronius, both from that most exalted seat, as they say, of worldly power, rose, the one to the name of religion, the other to that of the priesthood. And when shall I unroll from that great volume of numbers [the names of] those most distinguished in eloquence: Firmianus, Minucius, Cyprian, Hilary, John, Ambrose? These too, I believe, had said to themselves what one of our own says, when he was rousing himself, as if with this spur, from the world to this more blessed life; they had said, I believe: "What is this?"
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: 'eliam' for 'etiam', 'Jlilarius' for 'Hilarius', 'ltalia' for 'Italia', 'farundia' for 'facundia', 'Ililarium' for 'Hilarium'; the stray ';' after 'mundana' is ignored and 'mundanae potestatis' is read. Bracketed editorial notes in the text are not translated: one says Erasmus thinks 'Hilarium' should be replaced by 'Evagrium', and the other identifies John as Chrysostom. Firmianus is Lactantius and Minucius is Minucius Felix. The sentence beginning 'so passed over' completes a sentence about Paulinus of Nola that starts in the preceding context. 'One of our own' is Augustine; the words 'What is this?' echo Confessions 8.8, and the quotation continues in the following context.
